entries.1d00ff81ba1cf8401a28db579b0559efb5a1f52f: <div sID="gen2211" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="39" osisID="Exod.39" sID="Exod.39"/> <div eID="gen2211" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2212" type="x-p"/> This chapter gives us an account of the finishing of the work of the tabernacle. I. The last things prepared were the holy garments. The ephod and its curious girdle, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.1-Exod.39.5">ver. 1-5</reference>. The onyx-stones for the shoulders, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.6-Exod.39.7">ver. 6, 7</reference>. The breastplate with the precious stones in it, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.8-Exod.39.21">ver. 8-21</reference>. The robe of the ephod, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.22-Exod.39.26">ver. 22-26</reference>. The coats, bonnets, and breeches, for the inferior priests, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.27-Exod.39.29">ver. 27-29</reference>. And the plate of the holy crown, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.30-Exod.39.31">ver. 30, 31</reference>. II. A summary account of the whole work, as it was presented to Moses when it was all finished, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.32-Exod.39.43">ver. 32</reference>, &c.
entries.0db11cb1698b00c8b114ceee2b3a8c2964d9a601: <div eID="gen2212" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Tabernacle and Its Furniture. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1491.)</title> <div sID="gen2213" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made cloths of service, to do service in the holy <hi type="italic">place,</hi> and made the holy garments for Aaron; as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. <hi type="super">2</hi> And he made the ephod <hi type="italic">of</hi> gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen. <hi type="super">3</hi> And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut <hi type="italic">it into</hi> wires, to work <hi type="italic">it</hi> in the blue, and in the purple, and in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, <hi type="italic">with</hi> cunning work. <hi type="super">4</hi> They made shoulderpieces for it, to couple <hi type="italic">it</hi> together: by the two edges was it coupled together. 5 And the curious girdle of his ephod, that <hi type="italic">was</hi> upon it, <hi type="italic">was</hi> of the same, according to the work thereof; <hi type="italic">of</hi> gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen; as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. 6 And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel. <hi type="super">7</hi> And he put them on the shoulders of the ephod, <hi type="italic">that they should be</hi> stones for a memorial to the children of Israel; as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. 8 And he made the breastplate <hi type="italic">of</hi> cunning work, like the work of the ephod; <hi type="italic">of</hi> gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen. <hi type="super">9</hi> It was foursquare; they made the breastplate double: a span <hi type="italic">was</hi> the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof, <hi type="italic">being</hi> doubled. <hi type="super">10</hi> And they set in it four rows of stones: <hi type="italic">the first</hi> row <hi type="italic">was</hi> a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this <hi type="italic">was</hi> the first row. 11 And the second row, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond. <hi type="super">12</hi> And the third row, a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst. <hi type="super">13</hi> And the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: <hi type="italic">they were</hi> inclosed in ouches of gold in their inclosings. <hi type="super">14</hi> And the stones <hi type="italic">were</hi> according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, <hi type="italic">like</hi> the engravings of a signet, every one with his name, according to the twelve tribes. <hi type="super">15</hi> And they made upon the breastplate chains at the ends, <hi type="italic">of</hi> wreathen work <hi type="italic">of</hi> pure gold. <hi type="super">16</hi> And they made two ouches <hi type="italic">of</hi> gold, and two gold rings; and put the two rings in the two ends of the breastplate. <hi type="super">17</hi> And they put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate. <hi type="super">18</hi> And the two ends of the two wreathen chains they fastened in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod, before it. 19 And they made two rings of gold, and put <hi type="italic">them</hi> on the two ends of the breastplate, upon the border of it, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> on the side of the ephod inward. <hi type="super">20</hi> And they made two <hi type="italic">other</hi> golden rings, and put them on the two sides of the ephod underneath, toward the forepart of it, over against the <hi type="italic">other</hi> coupling thereof, above the curious girdle of the ephod. <hi type="super">21</hi> And they did bind the breastplate by his rings unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not be loosed from the ephod; as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. <hi type="super">22</hi> And he made the robe of the ephod <hi type="italic">of</hi> woven work, all <hi type="italic">of</hi> blue. <hi type="super">23</hi> And <hi type="italic">there was</hi> an hole in the midst of the robe, as the hole of an habergeon, <hi type="italic">with</hi> a band round about the hole, that it should not rend. <hi type="super">24</hi> And they made upon the hems of the robe pomegranates <hi type="italic">of</hi> blue, and purple, and scarlet, <hi type="italic">and</hi> twined <hi type="italic">linen.</hi> <hi type="super">25</hi> And they made bells <hi type="italic">of</hi> pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates upon the hem of the robe, round about between the pomegranates; 26 A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, round about the hem of the robe to minister <hi type="italic">in;</hi> as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. <hi type="super">27</hi> And they made coats <hi type="italic">of</hi> fine linen <hi type="italic">of</hi> woven work for Aaron, and for his sons, <hi type="super">28</hi> And a mitre <hi type="italic">of</hi> fine linen, and goodly bonnets <hi type="italic">of</hi> fine linen, and linen breeches <hi type="italic">of</hi> fine twined linen, <hi type="super">29</hi> And a girdle <hi type="italic">of</hi> fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, <hi type="italic">of</hi> needlework; as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. <hi type="super">30</hi> And they made the plate of the holy crown <hi type="italic">of</hi> pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, <hi type="italic">like to</hi> the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD. <hi type="super">31</hi> And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fasten <hi type="italic">it</hi> on high upon the mitre; as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses. <div eID="gen2213" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2214" type="x-p"/> In this account of the making of the priests' garments, according to the instructions given (ch. 28), we may observe, 1. That the priests' garments are called here <hi type="italic">clothes of service,</hi> <reference osisRef="Exod.39.1">v. 1</reference>. Note, Those that wear robes of honour must look upon them as clothes of service; for from those upon whom honour is put service is expected. It is said of those that are arrayed in white robes that they <hi type="italic">are before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.7.13">Rev. vii. 13, 15</reference>. Holy garments were not made for men to sleep in, or to strut in, but to do service in; and then they are indeed for glory and beauty. The Son of man himself <hi type="italic">came not to be ministered unto, but to minister.</hi> 2. That all the six paragraphs here, which give a distinct account of the making of these holy garments, conclude with those words, <hi type="italic">as the Lord commanded Moses,</hi> <reference osisRef="Exod.39.5 Exod.39.7 Exod.39.21 Exod.39.26 Exod.39.29 Exod.39.31">v. 5, 7, 21, 26, 29, 31</reference>. The like is not in any of the foregoing accounts, as if in these, more than any other of the appurtenances of the tabernacle, they had a particular regard to the divine appointment, both for warrant and for direction. It is an intimation to all the Lord's ministers to make the word of God their rule in all their ministrations, and to act in observance of and obedience to the command of God. 3. That these garments, in conformity to the rest of the furniture of the tabernacle, were very rich and splendid; the church in its infancy was thus taught, thus pleased, with the rudiments of this world; but now under the gospel, which is the ministration of the Spirit, to affect and impose such pompous habits as the church of Rome does, under pretence of decency and instruction, is to betray <hi type="italic">the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free,</hi> and to entangle the church again in the bondage of those carnal ordinances which were imposed only till the time of reformation. 4. That they were all shadows of good things to come, but the substance is Christ, and the grace of the gospel; when therefore the substance has come, it is a jest to be fond of the shadow. (1.) Christ is our great high-priest; when he undertook the work of our redemption, he put on the clothes of service—he arrayed himself with the gifts and graces of the Spirit, which he received not by measure—girded himself with the curious girdle of resolution, to go through with his undertaking—charged himself with the curious girdle of resolution, to go through with his undertaking—charged himself with all God's spiritual Israel, bore them on his shoulders, carried them in his bosom, laid them near his heart, engraved them on the palms of his hands, and presented them in the breast-plate of judgment unto his Father. And (lastly) he crowned himself with <hi type="italic">holiness to the Lord,</hi> consecrating his whole undertaking to the honour of his Father's holiness: now consider how great this man is. (2.) True believers are spiritual priests. The clean linen with which all their clothes of service must be made is <hi type="italic">the righteousness of saints</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rev.19.8">Rev. xix. 8</reference>), and <hi type="italic">Holiness to the Lord</hi> must be so written upon their foreheads that all who converse with them may see, and say, that they bear the image of God's holiness, and are devoted to the praise of it.
entries.378b4d07c514e611eba0c12bbd74e50feb019ce3: <div eID="gen2214" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Tabernacle Completed. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1491.)</title> <div sID="gen2215" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">32</hi> Thus was all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation finished: and the children of Israel did according to all that the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses, so did they. <hi type="super">33</hi> And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the tent, and all his furniture, his taches, his boards, his bars, and his pillars, and his sockets, <hi type="super">34</hi> And the covering of rams' skins dyed red, and the covering of badgers' skins, and the vail of the covering, <hi type="super">35</hi> The ark of the testimony, and the staves thereof, and the mercy seat, <hi type="super">36</hi> The table, <hi type="italic">and</hi> all the vessels thereof, and the showbread, <hi type="super">37</hi> The pure candlestick, <hi type="italic">with</hi> the lamps thereof, <hi type="italic">even with</hi> the lamps to be set in order, and all the vessels thereof, and the oil for light, <hi type="super">38</hi> And the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the hanging for the tabernacle door, <hi type="super">39</hi> The brazen altar, and his grate of brass, his staves, and all his vessels, the laver and his foot, <hi type="super">40</hi> The hangings of the court, his pillars, and his sockets, and the hanging for the court gate, his cords, and his pins, and all the vessels of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of the congregation, <hi type="super">41</hi> The cloths of service to do service in the holy <hi type="italic">place,</hi> and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons' garments, to minister in the priest's office. <hi type="super">42</hi> According to all that the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work. <hi type="super">43</hi> And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them. <div eID="gen2215" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2216" type="x-p"/> Observe here, I. The builders of the tabernacle made very good despatch. It was not much more than five months from the beginning to the finishing of it. Though there was a great deal of fine work about it, such as is usually the work of time, embroidering and engraving, not only in gold, but in precious stones, yet they went through with it in a little time. Church-work is usually slow work, but they made quick work of this, and yet did it with the greatest exactness imaginable. For, 1. Many hands were employed, all unanimous, and not striving with each other. This expedited the business, and made it easy. 2. The workmen were taught of God, and so were kept from making blunders, which would have retarded them. 3. The people were hearty and zealous in the work, and impatient till it was finished. God had prepared their hearts, and then <hi type="italic">the thing was done suddenly,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Chr.29.36">2 Chron. xxix. 36</reference>. Resolution and industry, and a cheerful application of mind, will, by the grace of God, bring a great deal of good work to pass in a little time, in less than one would expect. <div eID="gen2216" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2217" type="x-p"/> II. They punctually observed their orders, and did not in the least vary from them. They did it <hi type="italic">according to all that the Lord commanded Moses,</hi> <reference osisRef="Exod.39.32">v. 32</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.42">42</reference>. Note, God's work must be done, in every thing, according to his own will. His institutions neither need nor admit men's inventions to make them either more beautiful or more likely to answer the intention of them. <hi type="italic">Add thou not unto his words.</hi> God is pleased with willing worship, but not with will-worship. <div eID="gen2217" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2218" type="x-p"/> III. They brought all their work to Moses, and submitted it to his inspection and censure, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.33">v. 33</reference>. He knew what he had ordered them to make; and now the particulars were called over, and all produced, that Moses might see both that they had made all, omitting nothing, and that they had made all according to the instructions given them, and that, if they had made a mistake in any thing, it might be forthwith rectified. Thus they showed respect to Moses, who was set over them in the Lord; not objecting that Moses did not understand such work, and therefore that there was no reason for submitting it to his judgment. No, that God who gave them so much knowledge as to do the work gave them also so much humility as to be willing to have it examined and compared with the model. Moses was in authority, and they would pay a deference to his place. <hi type="italic">The spirit of the prophets is subject to the prophets.</hi> And besides, though they knew how to do the work better than Moses, Moses had a better and more exact idea of the model than they had, and therefore they could not be well pleased with their own work, unless they had his approbation. Thus in all the services of religion we should <hi type="italic">labour to be accepted of the Lord.</hi> <div eID="gen2218" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2219" type="x-p"/> IV. Moses, upon search, found all done according to the rule, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.43">v. 43</reference>. Moses, both for their satisfaction and for his own, did look upon all the work, piece by piece, and behold they had done it according to the pattern shown him, for the same Being that showed him the pattern guided their hand in the work. All the copies of God's grace exactly agree with the original of his counsels: what God works in us, and by us, is the fulfilling of the good pleasure of his own goodness; and when the mystery of God shall be finished, and all his performances come to be compared with his purposes, it will appear that behold all is done according to the counsel of his own will, not one iota or tittle of which shall fall to the ground, or be varied from. <div eID="gen2219" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2220" type="x-p"/> V. Moses blessed them. 1. He commended them, and signified his approbation of all they had done. He did not find fault where there was none, as some do, who think they disparage their own judgment if they do not find something amiss in the best and most accomplished performance. In all this work it is probable there might have been found here and there a stitch amiss, and a stroke awry, which would have served for an over-curious and censorious critic to animadvert upon; but Moses was too candid to notice small faults where there were no great ones. Note, All governors must be a praise to those that do well, as well as a terror to evil-doers. Why should any take a pride in being hard to be pleased? 2. He not only praised them, but prayed for them. He blessed them as one having authority, for the less is blessed of the better. We read not of any wages that Moses paid them for their work, but this blessing he gave them. For, though ordinarily the labourer be worthy of his hire, yet in this case, 1. They wrought for themselves. The honour and comfort of God's tabernacle among them would be recompence enough. <hi type="italic">If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself.</hi> 2. They had their meat from heaven on free-cost, for themselves and their families, and their raiment waxed not old upon them; so that they neither needed wages nor had reason to expect any. <hi type="italic">Freely you have received, freely give.</hi> The obligations we lie under, both in duty and interest, to serve God, should be sufficient to quicken us to our work, though we had not a reward in prospect. But, 3. This blessing, in the name of the Lord, was wages enough for all their work. Those whom God employs he will bless, and those whom he blesses are blessed indeed. The blessing he commands is <hi type="italic">life for evermore.</hi>  <chapter eID="Exod.39"/> <div eID="gen2220" type="x-p"/>

entries.6dfc7ab71bdeec996f807d012e6f2be4abf4b546: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv969"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 39</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Exod.39.1-Exod.39.43">Ex 39:1-43</reference>. Garments of the Priests.</title> <div sID="gen1338" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv969"/><hi type="bold">1-2. cloths of service--</hi>official robes. The ephod of the high priest, the robe of the ephod, the girdle of needlework, and the embroidered coat were all of fine linen; for on no material less delicate could such elaborate symbolical figures have been portrayed in embroidery, and all beautified with the same brilliant colors. (See on <reference osisRef="Exod.28.1-Exod.28.43">Ex 28:1-43</reference>). <div eID="gen1338" type="x-p"/>
entries.b9c325ffaa195ee528dbeb081030bc6123fd278c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv970"/><div sID="gen1339" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv970"/><hi type="bold">3. cut the gold into wires to work it--</hi>that is, the metal was beaten with a hammer into thin plates, cut with scissors or some other instrument into long slips, then rounded into filaments or threads. "Cloth of golden tissue is not uncommon on the monuments, and specimens of it have been found rolled about mummies; but it is not easy to determine whether the gold thread was originally interwoven or subsequently inserted by the embroiderer" [Taylor]. <div eID="gen1339" type="x-p"/>
entries.c8154dc07129789ecae2a038389cf0621cdf60ce: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv971"/><div sID="gen1340" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv971"/><hi type="bold">30. a writing, like to the engravings of a signet--</hi>The seal-ring worn both by ancient and modern Egyptians on the little finger of the right hand, contained, inscribed on a cornelian or other precious stone, along with the owner's name, a religious sentiment or sacred symbol, intimating that he was the servant of God, or expressive of trust in Him. And it was to this practice the inscription on the high priest alludes (compare <reference osisRef="John.3.33">Joh 3:33</reference>). <div eID="gen1340" type="x-p"/>
entries.661915c76158dbd8619f8205e9d1f5f17c72cf28: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv972"/><div sID="gen1341" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv972"/><hi type="bold">34. the covering of rams' skin dyed red--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Exod.25.5">Ex 25:5</reference>). It was probably red morocco leather and "badgers' skins," rather "the skins of the tahash, supposed to be the dugong, or dolphin of the Red Sea, the skin of which is still used by the Arabs under the same appellation" [Goss]. <div eID="gen1341" type="x-p"/>
entries.953f205d7da2678679df3da30bff2f5b02b5781b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv973"/><div sID="gen1342" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv973"/><hi type="bold">43. Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded--</hi>A formal inspection was made on the completion of the tabernacle, not only with a view to have the work transferred from the charge of the workmen, but to ascertain whether it corresponded with "the pattern." The result of a careful and minute survey showed that every plank, curtain, altar, and vase had been most accurately made of the form, and in the place designed by the Divine Architect--and Moses, in accepting it of their hands, thanked God for them, and begged Him to bless them. <chapter eID="Exod.39"/>

entries.a2b7190426167881c408237c65705b596ae00108: <div eID="gen4153" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen4154" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen4155" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen4155" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen4154" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen4156" type="x-p"/> Bezaleel makes the clothes of service for the holy place, and the holy garments, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.1">Exo 39:1</reference>. The ephod, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.2">Exo 39:2</reference>. Gold is beaten into plates, and cut into wires for embroidery, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.3">Exo 39:3</reference>. He makes the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.4">Exo 39:4</reference>. The curious girdle, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.5">Exo 39:5</reference>. Cuts the onyx stones for the shoulder-pieces, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.6">Exo 39:6</reference>. Makes the breastplate, its chains, ouches, rings, etc., <reference osisRef="Exo.39.7-Exo.39.21">Exo 39:7-21</reference>. The robe of the ephod, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.22-Exo.39.26">Exo 39:22-26</reference>. Coats of fine linen, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.27">Exo 39:27</reference>. The mitre, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.28">Exo 39:28</reference>. The girdle, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.29">Exo 39:29</reference>. The plate of the holy crown, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.30">Exo 39:30</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.31">Exo 39:31</reference>. The completion of the work of the tabernacle, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.32">Exo 39:32</reference>. All the work is brought unto Moses, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.33-Exo.39.41">Exo 39:33-41</reference>. Moses, having examined the whole, finds every thing done as the Lord had commanded in consequence of which he blesses the people, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.42">Exo 39:42</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exo.39.43">Exo 39:43</reference>. <div eID="gen4156" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4157" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen4157" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4158" type="x-p"/> Blue and purple, and scarlet - See this subject largely explained in the notes on <reference osisRef="Exo.25.4">Exo 25:4</reference> (note).
entries.7785cf4d22699dafdf501378867bb2f91396b7bc: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen4158" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4159" type="x-p"/> Ephod - See this described, <reference osisRef="Exo.25.7">Exo 25:7</reference> (note).
entries.1859ebb21b07000adada007eba577429ad0caf95: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen4159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4160" type="x-p"/> They did beat the gold into thin plates - For the purpose, as it is supposed, of cutting it into wires (פתילם) or threads; for to twist or twine is the common acceptation of the root פתל pathal. I cannot suppose that the Israelites had not then the art of making gold thread, as they possessed several ornamental arts much more difficult: but in the present instance, figures made in a more solid form than that which could have been effected by gold thread, might have been required.
entries.bb69c06a2eb456d6efdff2ecae6fc9e4a1b8f1ce: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen4160" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4161" type="x-p"/> Onyx stones - Possibly the Egyptian pebble. See <reference osisRef="Exo.25.7">Exo 25:7</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Exo.28.17">Exo 28:17</reference>, etc.
entries.5da387dc2c3ff26874bb19f109419537e7adeb26: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen4161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4162" type="x-p"/> Breastplate - See <reference osisRef="Exo.28.15">Exo 28:15</reference> (note).
entries.d92fa7566a4f10870bd98b7d74f431035becad33: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen4162" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4163" type="x-p"/> And they set in it four rows of stones - See all these precious stones particularly explained in the notes on <reference osisRef="Exo.28.17">Exo 28:17</reference> (note), etc.
entries.a83cbcce1b60433051dadb64654deaaa11577860: <hi type="bold">Verse 23</hi> <div eID="gen4163" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4164" type="x-p"/> As the hole of a habergeon - The habergeon or hauberk was a small coat of mail, something in form of a half shirt, made of small iron rings curiously united together. It covered the neck and breast, was very light, and resisted the stroke of a sword. Sometimes it went over the whole head as well as over the breast. This kind of defensive armor was used among the Asiatics, particularly the ancient Persians, among whom it is still worn. It seems to have been borrowed from the Asiatics by the Norman crusaders.
entries.85d9f2be35256039c2dba069432e35ae9c872263: <hi type="bold">Verse 30</hi> <div eID="gen4164" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4165" type="x-p"/> The holy crown of pure gold - On Asiatic monuments, particularly those that appear in the ruins of Persepolis and on many Egyptian monuments, the priests are represented as wearing crowns or tiaras, and sometimes their heads are crowned with laurel. Cuper observes, that the priests and priestesses, among the ancient Greeks, were styled στεφανοφοροι, or crown-bearers, because they officiated having sometimes crowns of gold, at others, crowns of laurel, upon their heads.
entries.dd9456162c83f30882e3e8c09133bdb758ed55a0: <hi type="bold">Verse 32</hi> <div eID="gen4165" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4166" type="x-p"/> Did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses - This refers to the command given <reference osisRef="Exo.25.40">Exo 25:40</reference>; and Moses has taken care to repeat every thing in the most circumstantial detail, to show that he had conscientiously observed all the directions he had received.
entries.6867d0e11c760820a9c4171ada7fd54c818aa8dd: <hi type="bold">Verse 37</hi> <div eID="gen4166" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4167" type="x-p"/> The pure candlestick - See Clarke's note on <reference osisRef="Exo.25.31">Exo 25:31</reference>. <div eID="gen4167" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4168" type="x-p"/> The lamps to be set in order - To be trimmed and fresh oiled every day, for the purpose of being lighted in the evening. See Clarke's note on <reference osisRef="Exo.27.21">Exo 27:21</reference>.
entries.52aea58ac803ba0c7318590f3b73f3384a3691fa: <hi type="bold">Verse 43</hi> <div eID="gen4168" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4169" type="x-p"/> And Moses did look upon all the work - As being the general superintendent of the whole, under whom Bezaleel and Aholiab were employed, as the other workmen were under them. <div eID="gen4169" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4170" type="x-p"/> They had done it as the Lord had commanded - Exactly according to the pattern which Moses received from the Lord, and which he laid before the workmen to work by. <div eID="gen4170" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4171" type="x-p"/> And Moses blessed them - Gave them that praise which was due to their skill, diligence, and fidelity. See this meaning of the original word in the note on <reference osisRef="Gen.2.3">Gen 2:3</reference> (note). See also a fine instance of ancient courtesy between masters and their servants, in the case of Boaz and his reapers, <reference osisRef="Rut.2.4">Rut 2:4</reference>. Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said to the reapers, The Lord be with You! And they answered him, The Lord bless Thee! It is, however, very probable that Moses prayed to God in their behalf, that they might be prospered in all their undertakings, saved from every evil, and be brought at last to the inheritance that fadeth not away. This blessing seems to have been given, not only to the workmen, but to all the people. The people contributed liberally, and the workmen wrought faithfully, and the blessing of God was pronounced upon All. <div eID="gen4171" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4172" type="x-p"/> The promptitude, cordiality, and dispatch used in this business cannot be too highly commended, and are worthy of the imitation of all who are employed in any way in the service of God. The prospect of having God to dwell among them inflamed every heart, because they well knew that on this depended their prosperity and salvation. They therefore hastened to build him a house, and they spared no expense or skill to make it, as far as a house made with hands could be, worthy of that Divine Majesty who had promised to take up his residence in it. This tabernacle, like the temple, was a type of the human nature of the Lord Jesus; that was a shrine not made with hands, formed by God himself, and worthy of that fullness of the Deity that dwelt in it. <div eID="gen4172" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4173" type="x-p"/> It is scarcely possible to form an adequate opinion of the riches, costly workmanship, and splendor of the tabernacle; and who can adequately conceive the glory and excellence of that human nature in which the fullness of the Godhead bodily dwelt? That this tabernacle typified the human nature of Christ, and the Divine shechinah that dwelt in it the Deity that dwelt in the man Christ Jesus, these words of St. John sufficiently prove: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (εσκηνωσεν εν ἡμιν, made his Tabernacle among us), full of grace and truth - possessing the true Urim and Thummim; all the lights and perfections, the truth and the grace, typified by the Mosaic economy, <reference osisRef="Joh.1.1">Joh 1:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Joh.1.14">Joh 1:14</reference>. And hence the evangelist adds, And we beheld his glory; as the Israelites beheld the glory of God resting on the tabernacle, so did the disciples of Christ see the Divine glory resting on him, and showing itself forth in all his words, spirit, and works. And for what purpose was the tabernacle erected? That God might dwell in it among the children of Israel. And for what purpose was the human nature of Christ so miraculously produced? That the Godhead might dwell in it; and that God and man might be reconciled through this wonderful economy of Divine grace, God being in Christ reconciling the world unto himself, <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.19">2Cor 5:19</reference>. And what was implied by this reconciliation? The union of the soul with God, and the indwelling of God in the soul. Reader, has God yet filled thy tabernacle with his glory? Does Christ dwell in thy heart by faith; and dost thou abide in him, bringing forth fruit unto holiness? Then thy end shall be eternal life. Why shouldst thou not go on thy way rejoicing with Christ in thy heart, heaven in thine eye, and the world, the devil, and the flesh, under thy feet?  <chapter eID="Exod.39"/> <div eID="gen4173" type="x-p"/>

entries.69d9962f4b734035fa25ff9804ce80d00457e1c2: <reference osisRef="Exod.39.1-Exod.39.31">Exo 39:1-31</reference> <hi type="italic">Preparation of the priests’ clothes</hi>. - Previous to the description of the dress itself, we have a statement in <reference osisRef="Exod.39.1">Exo 39:1</reference> of the materials employed, and the purpose to which they were devoted (“cloths of service,” see at <reference osisRef="Exod.31.10">Exo 31:10</reference>). The robes consisted of the <hi type="italic">ephod</hi> (<reference osisRef="Exod.39.2-Exod.39.7">Exo 39:2-7</reference>, as in <reference osisRef="Exod.28.6-Exod.28.12">Exo 28:6-12</reference>), the <hi type="italic">choshen</hi> or breastplate (<reference osisRef="Exod.39.8-Exod.39.21">Exo 39:8-21</reference>, as in <reference osisRef="Exod.28.15-Exod.28.29">Exo 28:15-29</reference>), the <hi type="italic">meïl</hi> or over-coat (<reference osisRef="Exod.39.22-Exod.39.26">Exo 39:22-26</reference>, as in <reference osisRef="Exod.28.31-Exod.28.34">Exo 28:31-34</reference>); the <hi type="italic">body-coats, turbans, drawers, and girdles,</hi> for Aaron and his sons (<reference osisRef="Exod.39.27-Exod.39.29">Exo 39:27-29</reference>, as in <reference osisRef="Exod.28.39-Exod.28.40">Exo 28:39-40</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Exod.28.42">Exo 28:42</reference>). The Urim and Thummim are not mentioned (cf. <reference osisRef="Exod.28.30">Exo 28:30</reference>). The head-dresses of the ordinary priests, which are simply called “bonnets” in <reference osisRef="Exod.28.40">Exo 28:40</reference>, are called “goodly bonnets” or “ornamental caps” in <reference osisRef="Exod.39.28">Exo 39:28</reference> of this chapter (מגבּעת פּארי, from פּאר an ornament, cf. פּאר <hi type="italic">ornatus fuit</hi>). The singular, “<hi type="italic">girdle</hi>,” in <reference osisRef="Exod.39.29">Exo 39:29</reference>, with the definite article, “<hi type="italic">the girdle,</hi>” might appear to refer simply to Aaron’s girdle, i.e., the girdle of the high priest; but as there is no special description of the girdles of Aaron’s sons (the ordinary priests) in <reference osisRef="Exod.29.40">Exo 29:40</reference>, where they are distinctly mentioned and called by the same name (<hi type="italic">abnet</hi>) as the girdle of Aaron himself, we can only conclude that they were of the same materials and the same form and make as the latter, and that the singular, האבנט, is used here either in the most general manner, or as a generic noun in a collective sense (see <hi type="italic">Ges.</hi> §109, 1). The last thing mentioned is the diadem upon Aaron’s turban (<reference osisRef="Exod.39.30">Exo 39:30</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.39.31">Exo 39:31</reference>, as in <reference osisRef="Exod.28.36-Exod.28.38">Exo 28:36-38</reference>), so that the order in which the priests’ robes are given here is analogous to the position in which the ark of the covenant and the golden altar stand to one another in the directions concerning the sacred things in ch. 25-30. “For just as all the other things are there placed between the holy ark and the golden altar as the two poles, so here all the rest of the priests’ robes are included between the shoulder-dress, the principal part of the official robes of the high priest, and the golden frontlet, the inscription upon which rendered it the most striking sign of the dignity of his office” (<hi type="italic">Baumgarten</hi>).
entries.03db9ea0bfe1304bf40f068e010efb8eeb3a75cb: <reference osisRef="Exod.39.32-Exod.39.36">Exo 39:32-36</reference> <hi type="italic">Delivery of the work to Moses</hi>. - The different things are again mentioned one by one. By “the tent,” in <reference osisRef="Exod.39.33">Exo 39:33</reference>, we are to understand the two tent-cloths, the one of purple and the other of goats’ hair, by which the <hi type="italic">dwelling</hi> (משׁכּן, generally rendered tabernacle) was made into a tent (אלה). From this it is perfectly obvious, that the variegated cloth formed the inner walls of the dwelling, or covered the boards on the inner side, and that the goats’ hair-cloth formed the other covering. Moreover it is also obvious, that this is the way in which האהל is to be understood, from the fact, that in the list of the things belonging to the ohel the first to be mentioned are the gold and copper hooks (<reference osisRef="Exod.26.6">Exo 26:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.26.11">Exo 26:11</reference>) with which the two halves of the drapery that formed the tent were joined together, and then after that the boards, bolts, pillars, and sockets, as though subordinate to the tent-cloths, and only intended to answer the purpose of spreading them out into a tent of dwelling.
entries.c24ca6668d4e5714b0ca58451e0aa61af6136ce8: <reference osisRef="Exod.39.37-Exod.39.39">Exo 39:37-39</reference> <div eID="gen1128" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1129" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">The lamps of the order,</hi>” i.e., the lamps set in order upon the candlestick. In addition to all the vessels of the sanctuary, shew-bread (<reference osisRef="Exod.39.36">Exo 39:36</reference>), holy oil for the candlestick and for anointing, and fragrant incense (<reference osisRef="Exod.39.38">Exo 39:38</reference>), were also prepared and delivered to Moses, - everything, therefore, that was required for the institution of the daily worship, as soon as the tabernacle was set up.
entries.a50a18163cd0f332430dd25a760c1b363800a53e: <reference osisRef="Exod.39.40-Exod.39.42">Exo 39:40-42</reference> <div eID="gen1129" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1130" type="x-p"/> “<hi type="italic">Vessels of service:</hi>” see Exo 27:19.
entries.fd9cd5ce4c3f41226979528fc459b812d6111b8e: <reference osisRef="Exod.39.43">Exo 39:43</reference> <div eID="gen1130" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1131" type="x-p"/> When Moses had received and examined all the different articles, and found that everything was made according to the directions of Jehovah, he blessed the children of Israel. The readiness and liberality with which the people had presented the gifts required for this work, and the zeal which they had shown in executing the whole of the work in rather less than half a year (see at <reference osisRef="Exod.40.17">Exo 40:17</reference>), were most cheering signs of the willingness of the Israelites to serve the Lord, for which they could not fail to receive the blessing of God. Call of Moses, and His Return to Egypt - Exodus 3 And 4 <div eID="gen1131" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1132" type="x-p"/> Call of Moses. - Whilst the children of Israel were groaning under the oppression of Egypt, God had already prepared the way for their deliverance, and had not only chosen Moses to be the saviour of His people, but had trained him for the execution of His designs.  <chapter eID="Exod.39"/> <div eID="gen1132" type="x-p"/>

entries.b4d8992333fe90b467979faa8a96396673732cb1: <div annotateRef="Bible:Exod.39.1" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Exod.39.1" sID="gen17338" type="section"/> <div sID="gen17339" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1. </hi><hi type="italic">And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet</hi>. The description of the sacerdotal garments, which is repeated in this chapter, is more accurate than it would have been had he been speaking of some unimportant matter. And assuredly, since Christ was vividly represented in the person of the high priest, this was a most important part of the legal service. We have elsewhere set forth how far it was from being an empty pomp, as when the Popish sacrificers now-a-days, in order to acquire dignity, dazzle the eyes of the simple by the splendor of their vestments, and their magnificent paraphernalia; but that rather it was for the purpose of placing before men’s eyes all that faith ought to consider in Jesus Christ. We have especially seen how great mysteries were contained in the mitre, which was Holiness to the Lord: and in the ephod, in which shone forth the light of truth and integrity of life, and in which were the symbols of the ten tribes, so that the priest bore the people itself upon his shoulders and before his breast, in such a manner that in the person of one all might be presented familiarly before God. For this reason he repeats seven times the clause, “as the Lord commanded Moses;” which certainly has the effect of awakening attention.<div eID="gen17339" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Exod.39.1" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen17338" osisID="Exod.39.1" type="section"/>

32. Thus was all the work of the tabernacle. A brief summary is now subjoined, whereby he indicates that in no part was there the least defect, and also declares that the children of Israel had so obeyed God’s commands, that the work itself varied in no respect from its pattern. “The children of Israel,” he says, “did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so did they;” whence we gather that no part of the building was impaired by any admixture. Afterwards it is added, that the tabernacle with its utensils and furniture was brought before Moses, and that all things were approved of by his judgment; for he is said to have “blessed them,” because they had duly and faithfully obeyed God’s command. This, however, was not a simple prayer, as of a private individual; but it was a promise of reward, such as might awaken confidence in the minds of the people, when they heard from the mouth (“D’un tel Prophete;” of such a Prophet. — Fr.) of this excellent and unimpeachable witness that their labor was pleasing to God.
Exodus 24
Exodus 24:1-18
1. And he said unto Moses, Come up unto the Lord, thou, and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship ye afar off.
1. Et dixit ad Mosen, Ascende ad Jehovam tu et Aharon, Nadab et Abihu, et septuaginta e senioribus Israel, et adorabitis procul.
2. And Moses alone shall come near the Lord; but they shall not come nigh, neither shall the people go up with him.
2. Solus autem Moses perveniet ad Jehovam: ipsi vero non pervenient, nec populus ascendet cum eo.
3. And Moses came and told the people all the words of the Lord, and all the judgments: and all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do.
3. Venit ergo Moses, et narravit populo omnia verba Jehovae, omniaque judicia, Et respondit totus populus una voce, ac dixerunt, Quaecunque verba loquutus est Jehova, faciemus.
4. And Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the hill, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
4. (Seripserat autem Moses omnia verba Jehovae): surgensque mane aedificavit altare sub monte, et duodecim statuas secundum duodecim tribus lsrael.
5. And he sent young men of the children of Israel, which offered burnt-offerings, and sacrificed peace-offerings of oxen unto the Lord.
5. Misitque juniores filiorum Israel, qui immolaverunt holocausta, et sacrificaverunt sacrificia prosperitatum ipsi Jehovae, vitulos.
6. And Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basins; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
6. Accepit Moses dimidium sanguinis, et posuit in crateribus: dimidium vero sanguinis sparsit super altare.
7. And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient.
7. Sumpsit deinde librum foederis, et legit in auribus populi: qui dixerunt, Quaecunque dixit Jehova, faciemus, et obediemus.
8. And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.
8. Tulit quoque Moses sanguinem, et sparsit super populum, ac dixit, Ecce, sanguis foederis quod pepigit Jehova vobiscum super cunctis his sermonibus.
9. Then went up Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel;
9. Ascendit autem Moses, et Aharon, Nadab et Abihu, et septuaginta e senioribus Israel.
10. And they saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire-stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.
10. Et viderunt Deum Israel: et sub pedibus ejus erat tanquam opus tabulae sapphiri, et sicut species coeli serenitate.
11. And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: also they saw God, and did eat and drink.
11. Et in principes filiorum Israel non extendit manum suam: et viderunt Deum, et comederunt, et biberunt.
12. And the Lord said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mount, and be there; and I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written; that thou mayest teach them.
12. Dixitque Jehova ad Mosen, Ascende ad me in montem, et esto ibi; daboque tibi duas tabulas lapideas, et Legem atque praeceptum, quae scripsi ad docendum eos.
13. And Moses rose up, and his minister Joshua; and Moses went up into the mount of God.
13. Surrexit itaque Moses et Jehosua minister ejus; et ascendit Moses in montem Dei.
14. And he said unto the elders, Tarry ye here for us, until we come again unto you: and, behold, Aaron and Hur are with you: if any man have any matters to do, let him come unto them.
14. Senioribusque dixit, Manete hic donec revertamur ad vos: et ecce, Aharon et Hur sunt vobiscum: quisquis habuerit causas, accedet ad eos.
15. And Moses went up into the mount, and a cloud covered the mount.
15. Tunc ascendit Moses in montem, et operuit nubes montem.
16. And the glory of the Lord abode upon mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days: and the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud.
16. Habitavitque gloria Jehovae; super montem Sinai, et operuit eum nubes sex diebus: vocavitque ipsum Mosen die septimo e medio nubis.
17. And the sight of the glory of the Lord was like devouring fire on the top of the mount in the eyes of the children of Israel.
17. Et aspectus gloriae Jehovae erat tanquam ignis comburens in vertice montis, in oculis filiorum Israel.
18. And Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and gat him up into the mount: and Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights.
18. Et ingressus est Moses in medium nubis, ascenditque in montem: et fuit Moses in monte quadraginta diebus, et quadraginta noctibus.

entries.7231517a369e8e2e1c50670877cf68031e9f710f:
<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39" type="chapter">
                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXXIX.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 AND of the blue, and purple, and scarlet they made clothes of service, to do ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vice in the holy <ns0:hi>place,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 31. 10. and 35. 19.</ns0:note> made the holy gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments for Aaron, as the LORD commanded Moses.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And he made the ephod <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut <ns0:hi>it into</ns0:hi> wiers, to work <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> in the blue, and in the purple, and in the scarlet, and in the fine linnen <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> cunning work.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 They made shoulder pieces for it, to couple <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> together: by the two edges was it coupled to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gether.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And the curious girdle of his ephod that <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> upon it <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> of the same, according to the work thereof, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, as the LORD commanded Moses.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 28. 9.</ns0:note> And they wrought onyx-stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And he put them on the shoulders of the Ephod, <ns0:hi>that they should be</ns0:hi> stones for a <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 28. 12.</ns0:note> memorial to the children of Israel, as the LORD command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed Moses.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And he made the breast-plate <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> cunning work like the work <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> the ephod, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet and fine twined linen.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 It was foursquare, they made the brest-plate double: a span <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof <ns0:hi>being</ns0:hi> doubled.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And they set in it four rows of stones: the <ns0:hi>first</ns0:hi> row <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> Ruby.</ns0:note> Sardius, a Topaz, and a Carbun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cle: this <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> the first row.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And the second row an Emeraud, a Saphir, and a Diamond.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And the third row a Ligure, an Agate, and an Amethyst.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And the fourth row a Beryl, an onyx, and a Jasper: <ns0:hi>they were</ns0:hi> inclosed in ouches of gold in their inclosings.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And the stones <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the ingravings of a signet, every one with his name according to the twelve Tribes.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And they made upon the Brest-plate chains at the ends, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> wreathen work <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> pure gold.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 And they made two ouches <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> gold, and two gold rings: and put the two rings in the two ends of a brest-plate.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And they put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings on the ends of the brest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plate.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And the two ends of the two wreathen chains they fastned in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulder-pieces of the Ephod before it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And they made two rings of gold, and put <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> on the two ends of the breast-plate upon the border of it, which <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> on the side of the Ephod inward.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And they made two <ns0:hi>other</ns0:hi> golden rings, and put them on the two sides of the Ephod under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neath, toward the fore-part of it, over-against the <ns0:hi>other</ns0:hi> coupling thereof, above the curious gir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dle of the Ephod.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And they did bind the brest-plate by his rings unto the rings of the Ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be above the curious girdle of the Ephod, and that the brest-plate might not be loosed from the Ephod, as the LORD command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed Moses.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 And he made the robe of the Ephod of woven work, all <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> blue.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 And <ns0:hi>there was</ns0:hi> a hole in the midst of the robe, as the hole of an habergeon, <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> a band round about the hole, that it should not rent.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 And they made upon the hems of the robe, pomegranates <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> blue, and purple, and scarlet, and twined <ns0:hi>linen.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 And they made <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 28. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note> bels <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> pure gold, and put the bels between the pomegranates, upon the hem of the robe, round about between the pomegra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nates.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate round about the hem of the robe to minister <ns0:hi>in,</ns0:hi> as the LORD commanded Moses.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 And they made coats <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> fine linen <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> woven work, for Aaron and for his sons,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 And a mitre <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> fine linen, and goodly bonnets <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> fine linen, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 28. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:note> linen breeches <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> fine twined linen,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29 And a girdle <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> needle-work; as the LORD commanded Moses.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30 And they made the plate of the holy crown <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, <ns0:hi>like to</ns0:hi> the ingravings of a signet, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 28. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:note> HOLINESS TO THE LORD.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sten <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> on high upon the mitre; as the LORD commanded Moses.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="32">32 Thus was all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation finished: and the children of Israel did according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so did they.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="33">33 And they brought the tabernacle unto Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses, the tent, and all his furniture, his taches, his boards, his bars, and his pillars, and his sockets.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="34">34 And the covering of rams skins died red, and the covering of badgers skins, and the vail of the covering.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="35">35 The ark of the testimony, and the staves thereof, and the mercy-seat,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="36">36 The table <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> all the vessels thereof, and the shew-bread,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="37">37 The pure candlestick, <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> the lamps thereof, <ns0:hi>even with</ns0:hi> the lamps, to be set in or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der, and all the vessels thereof, and the oyl for light,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="38">38 And the golden altar, and the anointing oyl, and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> the in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cense of sweet spices.</ns0:note> the sweet incense, and the hanging for the tabernacle-door.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="39">39 The brazen altar, and his grate of brass, his staves, and all his vessels, the laver, and his feet,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="40">40 The hangings of the court, his pillars, and his sockets, and the hanging for the court-gate,
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:85" />
his cords, and his pins, and all the vessels of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of the con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gregation,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="41">41 The cloaths of service to do service in the holy <ns0:hi>place,</ns0:hi> and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons garments to minister in the priests office.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="42">42 According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="43">43 And Moses did look upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the LORD had com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Both the people for their liberal contribution, and the workmen for their great care and industry.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
